author: ValWood
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**


GO:0006801 | superoxide metabolic process | IEA with IPR036423 | GO_REF:0000002

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC22E12.04 ccs1 (copper chaperone)

* **Description of issue**

css1 is involved in the maturation of superoxide dismtase and so it is upstream of "superoxide metabolic process"
title: InterPro2GO issue: GO:0006801	 superoxide metabolic process IEA with IPR036423	GO_REF:0000002

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Val,
Thank you very much. In this case, this is a Homologous superfamily type of entry, which usually include a lot of sequences, and we tend/try not to add GO terms as they may not apply for all members. In this example, there are some viral proteins, with no enzymatic activity included in the the entry (for example: O57246), so I think it would be safer to remove GO:0006801 from it. I can create a Pfam domain for CCS1 as I can see it is missing. Does this make sense? Would that work? 
Best wishes
Sara

author: sarach06
body:
Hi Val,
I created a new Pfam entry for the proteins mentioned above. It will be available in Pfam release 38.3.

Best wishes
Sara
